subject: Post-call: Streamline Works usage review, renewal + pilot next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@streamlineworks.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: usage, pain, pilot options

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone (internal + external) has the same next steps. I tried to keep this tight.

Key points we heard
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference costs on peak batch jobs (data transform pipeline spikes) leading to budget overruns and throttled features.
- Secondary pain: occasional latency spikes during end-of-day scoring that impact SLAs to downstream teams.
- Current footprint: ~450k tokens/day (Q3 avg) but spikes up to ~1.8M on end-of-month runs; most heavy requests are long-context rerank and batch scoring.
- Current contract: hosted API pilot, no reserved capacity today.

Goals discussed
- Stabilize end-of-day latency to <150ms p95 for scoring flows.
- Reduce per-token unit cost for batch scoring by ~30% year-over-year.
- Run a 6-week pilot of Redwood Dedicated with a constrained reserved pool to validate cost and latency in production.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Redwood to send initial usage export + suggested Dedicated sizing and cost delta (owner: me) — by 2026-11-20. [attached: usage_report_q3.csv]
2) Streamline to confirm pilot scope (which models / flows, expected QPS during end-of-month) and internal pilot success criteria (Ellen / Sam) — by 2026-11-24.
3) Procurement review of draft SLA/terms (Procurement team) — Streamline to share feedback; we can provide a simplified redline if helpful.
4) If scope aligns, Redwood to provision a reserved pool for a 6-week pilot and schedule a kickoff.

Open questions we flagged
- Will the pilot include access to your production KV cache for prefix reuse, or will we run only a shadowed workload?
- Any compliance evidence (SOC2 artifacts) you need ahead of procurement sign-off? Rafael, happy to run the SOC2 pack.

Attachments: usage_report_q3.csv (summary export)

If that matches your view, I’ll send the Dedicated sizing and a rough cost delta this Friday and attach a short pilot statement of work.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for engineering teams
From: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@streamlineworks.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Li <sam.li@streamlineworks.com>, Procurement <procurement@streamlineworks.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: usage, pain, pilot options

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming on our side:
- Pilot scope: end-of-month scoring + nightly rerank batches (these two flows account for ~85% of the cost spikes).
- Success criteria: p95 latency <150ms during end-of-month for scoring; pilot must show a cost improvement >=25% over our current hosted usage baseline.
- We will aim to provide sample QPS numbers and a short test dataset by 2026-11-23. Sam will coordinate.

Procurement note: we have a standard PO/contract timeline of ~3 weeks once terms are clear. I’m looping procurement here so they can flag any must-have contract items early.

Quick Q: do you expect any downtime during Reserved pool provisioning? We need to avoid interruption to production scoring (we can run pilot in parallel if needed).

—Ellen
Ellen Shaw | Head of ML Platforms, Streamline Works
ellen.shaw@streamlineworks.com | +1 (415) 777-2010

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: usage, pain, pilot options

Hi Ellen / Sam / Procurement —

Following up with the deliverables we discussed. Attached: usage_report_q3.csv and a preliminary SLA/terms doc (redwood_sla_draft.pdf). Rafael and I put together two pilot options as discussed. Short summary below and links to next artifacts.

Pilot option highlights
- Option A (Dedicated pilot): 6-week reserved pool sized at 2 x p4d equivalent capacity during peak windows; estimated cost delta +12% vs current hosted list but projected net unit cost improvement of ~32% after KV caching + batching. Includes a 20% pilot discount and SLA coverage for p95 latency.
- Option B (Hosted + priority bursts): 6-week window with priority routing and batch pricing for end-of-month windows; minimal setup time, 8–12% projected cost improvement, no reserved capacity commitment.

Requested immediate next steps
1) Ellen/Sam: confirm which option you prefer and share the scoped dataset/QPS by Monday 2026-11-23.
2) Procurement: if you can share any required contract clauses, we will return a redline within 48 hours.
3) Redwood: we will provision a non-production parallel pool for smoke tests so there is zero impact on your production scoring. (No downtime expected.)

Doc links / actions
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/4321
- SOW draft & SLA (attached): redwood_sla_draft.pdf
- Internal pilot notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/s/streamline-workshop-notes

If that works, I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for next week and include Rafael to walk through the SOW and expected metrics to collect during the pilot.

Best —
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
